title: Long unbroken strings (URLs) in flex layouts cause horizontal page overflow
answers: Why does the page scroll sideways when a datasource error shows?
Long error message with a URL widens the panel/page
Query error text overflows its container instead of wrapping
How to fix flex item growing past its parent due to long unbreakable text
body:
Symptom: A datasource/query error containing a long unbroken string (typically a request URL with no spaces) widens its row/panel and causes the whole page to scroll horizontally.
Root cause: The error text container is a flex item with flex: 1 but no min-width override; browsers default a flex item's min-width to its content's min-content width, and a string with no break points has min-content width equal to its full length, so the item (and its ancestors) can't shrink below that.
Fix pattern: On the text element, set minWidth: 0 to remove the implicit flex min-width floor, and overflowWrap: 'anywhere' (not just word-break) to allow mid-word breaking for unbreakable tokens like URLs.
Constraints: Apply this to any flex/grid child rendering arbitrary/unbounded text (error messages, URLs, stack traces); not needed for text known to be short or already wrapped in a block (non-flex) container.
applies: Any flex-layout component rendering long, space-less text such as error messages/URLs in Grafana's query editor or similar shared components.
